newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GRETZKY HAS FOUR-POINT GAME AS RANGERS END SLIDE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-GRETZKY HAS FOUR-POINT GAME AS RANGERS END SLIDE.

text.p: Wayne Gretzky slipped into his "the Great One" persona on Sunday to help his new team halt a three-game losing streak.
Gretzky scored a goal and set up three more to lead the New York Rangers to a 6-4 win over the Buffalo Sabres.
Gretzky extended his point-scoring streak to 11 games with the 213th four-point game of his illustrious career.
The league's all-time leading scorer assisted on goals by Brian Leetch and Luc Robitaille 94 seconds apart in the first period to stake the Rangers to a 2-0 lead.
Mark Messier increased the lead to 3-0 with just over three minutes left in the opening period when he bounced a shot in off Buffalo goaltender Andrei Trefilov.
Buffalo cut the deficit to 3-2 early in the second period when Dan Plante and Michael Grosek beat Glenn Healy, who also allowed two late goals before finishing with 29 saves.
Gretzky restored the two-goal margin with his fifth goal of the season when his slap shot trickled underneath Trefilov's pads.
His assist on Niklas Sundstrom's powerplay goal in the final minute of the second period gave the Rangers a 6-2 lead.
"We played better tonight," said Messier. "Everybody did their job tonight. The bangers banged and the scorers scored."
In Chicago, Owen Nolan recorded his ninth career hat trick and Darren Turcotte scored twice in a five-goal first period outburst as the San Jose Sharks downed the Blackhawks 6-2.
Ulf Dahlen, Turcotte and Nolan scored 87 seconds apart, turning a 1-1 game into a 4-1 San Jose lead.
Nolan picked up his second of the game at 18:40 of the first and completed the hat trick with his sixth goal of the season 6:44 into the third.
"I'm just trying to throw the puck at the net and it seems to be going in for me," said Nolan, who also had an assist for a four-point game.
Kelly Hrudey made 25 saves for the Sharks, who picked up seven points on a 3-2-1 road trip.
Eric Daze and Alexei Zhamnov scored for the Blackhawks, who had allowed just nine goals in their previous five games.
In Philadelphia, John Vanbiesbrouck made 21 saves and Bill Lindsay's third-period goal proved the game winner as the Florida Panthers edged the Flyers 3-2 to remain the league's lone unbeaten team.
Scott Mellanby and Dave Lowry scored in the middle period for the Panthers, who improved to 7-0-3 and have outscored their opposition 35-17.

Lindsay whipped a wrist shot through Flyer goaltender Ron Hextall's pads 3:29 into the third period to extend Florida's lead to 3-1. The goal proved necessary when Daniel Lacroix beat Vanbiesbroiuck less than four minutes later to make it a one-goal game.
The Flyers stormed the Florida zone in the final minutes but were repeatedly turned away by Vanbiesbrouck, who stopped John LeClair's stuff attempt with 3:33 remaining to preserve the victory.
In Anaheim, Dave Gagner scored twice, including a goal with 4:46 left in the second period that snapped a tie, as the Calgary Flames skated to a 4-1 victory over the Mighty Ducks.
Gagner was just in the right place on his first goal. Jarome Iginla took a wrist shot from the right circle that deflected off Gagner's skate past goaltender Guy Hebert for a 2-1 lead.
Todd Hlushko and Gagner scored 28 seconds apart early in the third period to make it 4-1 as the Flames handed the Mighty Ducks a franchise-record seventh consecutive defeat.
Keven Todd's second-period goal for Anaheim ruined the shutout for Rick Tabaracci, who made 33 saves.
